transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Liam Ortega (Redwood AE), Jin Park (Redwood SE), Tanya Ruiz (MosaicX Lead Eng), Mark Chen (MosaicX Infra), Priya Kapoor (MosaicX CTO)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
- Hands-on integration walkthrough of Redwood SDKs (Python + TypeScript), focus on auth, environment variables, CI secret rotation, and quick sandbox start.
- Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private for MosaicX regulatory needs; security checklist requested.
- Agreed to provide sandbox keys and run an initial latency/cost benchmark; follow-up POC kickoff planned.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Liam): hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
00:04 Speaker 2 (Priya): yes loud and clear, thanks Liam
00:06 Speaker 1 (Liam): great cool uh quick intro i'm liam i'm the AE on the account jin is our se will do the deep parts, picnic we'll go through a short lab, will keep it pragmatic.
00:18 Speaker 3 (Jin): hi all, i'll lead the SDK part, we want to show both python and typescript snippets and then a quick run inside your sandbox. there will be a couple of infra calls about keys and vpc.
00:31 Speaker 4 (Tanya): sounds good, our main ask is to get something running in our dev cluster and verify latency/cost tradeoffs. also need to confirm we can do KMS-backed key management and SSO.
00:44 Speaker 2 (Priya): and timeline wise we want a two week POC end-to-end, maybe start faust next week.
00:50 Speaker 1 (Liam): perfect, we'll aim for 2-week POC kickoff, jin will share the security pack.

01:05 Speaker 3 (Jin): ok i'll switch to screen, starting with the python quickstart. first step is pip install redwood-inference (note: package name in demo is shorthand, actual pip name is redwood-sdk).
01:20 Speaker 3 (Jin): code snippet: from redwood import RedwoodClient  # pseudo import, we'll paste full snippet in the notes
01:28 Speaker 4 (Tanya): quick question, how do we pass api keys in CI securely? we use GitHub actions and Hashi vault.
01:36 Speaker 3 (Jin): good question. we recommend env vars in CI that reference secrets in your vault. e.g. REDWOOD_API_KEY as a repo secret, and avoid checking it into dotenv. for private/enterprise customers you can also use short-lived tokens via our token service integrated with your idp.
01:53 Speaker 5 (Mark): is there a recommended rotation cadence? we have strict policies for keys rotated every 7 days.
02:01 Speaker 3 (Jin): we support programmatic key rotation and the SDK honors short-lived creds. we can add the automation snippet to the checklist.

02:20 Speaker 3 (Jin): switching to TypeScript quickstart: npm install @redwood/inference --save, then import RedClient from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new RedClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
02:39 Speaker 4 (Tanya): and if we want to run against your hosted api vs our dedicated cluster, is the endpoint different?
02:46 Speaker 3 (Jin): yes endpoint changes. hosted is api.redwood.ai, dedicated will have a customer-specific endpoint and private on-prem uses a private control plane URL. we'll include exact endpoints in the email.

03:05 Speaker 1 (Liam): can you show the console briefly — model selection, routes, and the Optimize suggestions?
03:11 Speaker 3 (Jin): sure, quick walk — console has per-route latency and token cost, the optimize tab suggests batching configs and quantization profiles based on workload traces.
03:25 Speaker 4 (Tanya): we have lots of short prompts with avg 64 tokens but occasional 2k long responses, how does batching affect tail latency?
03:35 Speaker 3 (Jin): there's a trade-off — batching helps cost for short requests but can add a few ms to p99; we can set a max wait window and priority lanes for latency-sensitive routes. also automatic fallback to a faster/cheaper variant if under load.

04:02 Speaker 5 (Mark): can we do VPC peering to your hosted network or do we need private? we have stringent data residency.
04:11 Speaker 3 (Jin): for strict residency and network isolation we recommend Private (VPC/on-prem). Hosted supports VPC egress but not peering into our control plane; Dedicated offers more isolation but still in our infra. we'll share the matrix in the security doc.

04:35 Speaker 2 (Priya): show us an auth example with SAML SSO and role mappings? we assign RBAC roles per team.
04:42 Speaker 3 (Jin): in the console you can map SAML groups to Redwood roles; for private install we accept your IdP metadata. we'll include sample SAML metadata and a JSON snippet for role mapping.

05:10 Speaker 3 (Jin): demo time — i'm going to run the python quickstart in the sandbox project i provisioned earlier. command: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_abc123 (we'll not use real keys in transcript). then python run_quickstart.py
05:27 Speaker 3 (Jin): running now — the snippet hits the /v1/generate endpoint with a simple prompt and streams tokens back. note: streaming is optional in SDKs and uses chunked responses.
05:40 Speaker 4 (Tanya): are streaming payloads authenticated the same way? any different socket behavior?
05:46 Speaker 3 (Jin): same auth header but streaming uses a websocket or SSE path depending on client. we have examples for both languages.
06:02 Speaker 6 (Tanya, overlapping): and the kv cache — do you persist per-tenant or per-session? we want to reuse context across short lived sessions.
06:11 Speaker 3 (Jin): the runtime supports KV cache for prefixes and per-session caching; in hosted mode we maintain tenant-level cache with TTLs and encryption at rest. sometimes transcription will say K-V cash in the logs — internal misheard token.

07:00 Speaker 1 (Liam): switching gears to CI/CD, what do we need to wire for canary & rollouts?
07:06 Speaker 3 (Jin): you create routes in the console, each route can have rollout policies: canary traffic %, header-based routing, or user-segment routing. rollbacks are automatic on perf regressions if you enable the safety gates.
07:22 Speaker 5 (Mark): how are regressions detected — semantic evals or perf only?
07:28 Speaker 3 (Jin): both. we have evaluation hooks to run prompt sets and monitor quality regressions, and perf/tracing to catch latency spikes. you can tie alerts to PagerDuty as well.

08:00 Speaker 4 (Tanya): regarding cost measurement, do you break down per-token costs by model and include batching effects?
08:07 Speaker 3 (Jin): yes console shows token-level breakdown and an effective cost-per-output token factoring batching; Optimize suggests batch sizes to hit your target per-token cost.

08:35 Speaker 2 (Priya): we want to test a scenario: main product queries with sensitive pii, must not be logged. can we disable logs for select routes and have audit logs for admin only?
08:46 Speaker 3 (Jin): yes, route-level logging controls. you can disable request logging and still keep audit logs for admin events. for private deployments you can also forward logs to your SIEM.

09:10 Speaker 3 (Jin): back to the code, i'm switching to a quick Typescript demo for streaming and tool-calling. snippet: const resp = await client.chat.create({ model: 'rwd-chat-1', messages: [...] }); resp.stream((token)=> console.log(token));
09:28 Speaker 4 (Tanya): do you support function calling like output schemas? we need to validate structured responses.
09:34 Speaker 3 (Jin): yes structured output is supported; you can pass a jsonSchema and the runtime will attempt to enforce format and provide decoding helpers in the SDK.

10:05 Speaker 5 (Mark): anything we should watch for in containerized workloads — e.g., GPU assignment or kernel compat?
10:12 Speaker 3 (Jin): if you self-host, we provide a helm chart with nodeSelector hints; runtime will pick optimized kernels based on model/seq length. for dedicated we select kernels automatically but can pin quantization/ops if you need reproducible perf.

10:45 Speaker 1 (Liam): ok let's talk about the POC scope briefly - high level we propose: 2 week POC, objectives: validate latency p95 < 250ms for avg workload, cost target $X per 1k queries, confirm SSO+KMS integration, and a small integration in your dev app.
11:05 Speaker 2 (Priya): that sounds right, we'll refine the numbers. also need legal sign-off for data retention.
11:12 Speaker 1 (Liam): our legal will send a short addendum about retention defaults and options.

11:30 Speaker 3 (Jin): quick note on benchmarking — we'll provide a small bench harness sample (python/ts) that can replay your trace or synthetic load. please give your sample trace shape (seq length distribution, concurrency) and we'll run it in the sandbox.
11:50 Speaker 4 (Tanya): will do, i'll extract a representative one from prod logs, sanitize pii.

12:10 Speaker 3 (Jin): i'm pasting a couple of links in the chat (auto-transcript note: links not clickable here):
- SDK quickstart (python/ts): https://console.redwood.ai/sdk-quickstart
- Security & private deploy checklist: https://console.redwood.ai/enterprise/security-checklist
- POC runbook + bench harness: https://console.redwood.ai/poc/runbook

12:42 Speaker 5 (Mark): any gotchas with tokenization differences across models? we use char-level truncation and want consistent billing numbers.
12:52 Speaker 3 (Jin): different model families have different tokenizers; console normalizes token accounting per model but for cross-model experiments we recommend a fixed tokenization step in the bench harness to compare apples-to-apples.

13:15 Speaker 2 (Priya): competitors question: we evaluated OpenAI and Anthropic — what are main differences versus Redwood?
13:23 Speaker 3 (Jin): Redwood focuses on serving and ops — unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, optimize tooling for batching/caching, and predictable SLAs on Dedicated. for model capability you can pick curated open weights or bring-your-own-model.

13:45 Speaker 4 (Tanya): final quick technical: for short-lived tokens with your idp, do you support OIDC exchange flow?
13:51 Speaker 3 (Jin): yes OIDC exchange and token introspection endpoints are supported in private and dedicated installs. we'll include example config.

14:10 Speaker 1 (Liam): cool let's wrap with next steps and owners — jin, can you send the security pack and checklist?
14:17 Speaker 3 (Jin): yes will send by Friday.
14:19 Speaker 1 (Liam): i'll provision the sandbox and send API key to Tanya via secure channel by EOD tomorrow.
14:25 Speaker 4 (Tanya): thanks, i'll prepare the trace and share by Monday.
14:28 Speaker 2 (Priya): schedule 1 hour POC kickoff for next Tuesday if that works for liam and jin.
14:34 Speaker 1 (Liam): works for us, i'll propose a few times in the calendar.

Closing
14:45 Speaker 1 (Liam): thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the checklist, bench harness and schedule.
14:50 Speaker 4 (Tanya): appreciate it, excited to get started.
14:53 Speaker 2 (Priya): thanks all.

(end of transcript)
